prompt:
You are an associate analyst on the industrials and consumer coverage team at Brennan Brothers & Co. On May 13, 2026, Managing Director Kara Vossberg asked you to build a Q1 2026 budget vs. actual variance analysis for Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) following the company's May 6 10-Q filing. This will support the firm's ongoing coverage update and feed directly into the Monday sales desk call.

Pull the actual reported Q1 2026 figures from the EDGAR filing: Revenue came in at $181,519M, COGS at $87,463M, Operating Income at $23,852M, Net Income at $90,798M, and EPS (diluted) at $2.78 per share. Balance sheet snapshots as of March 31, 2026 show Total Assets of $916,630M, Stockholders' Equity of $441,914M, and Cash & Cash Equivalents of $101,816M. You'll note the XBRL data includes a Gross Profit figure of $5,531M — that tag is sourced from a 2009 filing artifact and should be excluded; derive Gross Profit correctly as Revenue minus COGS instead.

Build the deliverable as an Excel workbook with full formula transparency. Your variance table should compare Brennan Brothers' prior Q1 2026 estimates against these actuals across all nine line items listed above, with columns for absolute dollar variance, percentage variance, and a flag for any item exceeding ±5%. For flagged items, add a one-sentence driver explanation pulled from management commentary in the 10-Q or inferable from the financials. Where publicly available consensus mean estimates exist, include them as a third comparison column. All dollar figures in millions, one decimal place, standard sell-side formatting — blue font for hardcoded inputs, black for calculated, no merged cells in data ranges. Include a Revenue-minus-COGS reconciliation bridge for both estimate and actual to confirm Gross Profit consistency. Present EPS on a per-share basis and reconcile any share count difference between your estimate and the filing.

Use the attached AMZN_historical_financials.xlsx as reference for Brennan Brothers' original estimates and historical context. The executive summary at the top should call out the three largest absolute-dollar variances in a single paragraph that Kara can forward directly to clients.

rubric.criterion: Deliverable is provided as a single Excel (.xlsx) workbook file.
Workbook contains a sheet labeled 'Variance Analysis' or equivalent main analysis sheet.
Variance table includes all nine specified line items: Revenue, COGS, Gross Profit, Operating Income, Net Income, EPS (diluted), Total Assets, Stockholders' Equity, and Cash & Cash Equivalents.
Actual Revenue figure is stated as $181,519 million (or $181,519.0M).
Actual COGS figure is stated as $87,463 million (or $87,463.0M).
Actual Gross Profit is correctly calculated as Revenue minus COGS, yielding $94,056.0 million (not the stale XBRL value of $5,531M).
Actual Operating Income figure is stated as $23,852 million (or $23,852.0M).
Actual Net Income figure is stated as $90,798 million (or $90,798.0M).
Actual EPS (diluted) is stated as $2.78 per share, consistent with the 10-Q filing.
Actual Total Assets figure is stated as $916,630 million (or $916,630.0M).
Actual Stockholders' Equity figure is stated as $441,914 million (or $441,914.0M).
Actual Cash & Cash Equivalents figure is stated as $101,816 million (or $101,816.0M).
All dollar figures are displayed in millions (USD) with one decimal place.
Absolute dollar variance is calculated for each line item (Actual minus Estimate).
Percentage variance is calculated for each line item.
Line items where percentage variance exceeds ±5% are flagged (e.g., with highlighting, a flag column, or notation).
For each flagged line item (variance >±5%), a one-sentence driver explanation is provided, sourced from management commentary or identifiable from financials.
A reconciliation bridge is included showing Gross Profit = Revenue - COGS for both the Brennan Brothers estimate and the actual figures.
The reconciliation bridge demonstrates internal consistency (Actual GP = $181,519.0M - $87,463.0M = $94,056.0M).
EPS diluted is presented on a per-share basis consistent with the filing's $2.78/share figure.
Any share count difference between estimate and actual is reconciled or discussed.
An executive summary paragraph appears at the top of the deliverable summarizing the three largest absolute-dollar variances.
The executive summary is written in a client-forward-ready tone suitable for direct inclusion in an email.
A consensus sell-side mean estimate column is included where publicly available, enabling a three-way comparison (Brennan Brothers vs. Consensus vs. Actual).
Blue font is used for hardcoded input cells and black font for calculated cells, per Brennan Brothers template conventions.
No merged cells are used in the data range of the variance table.
Variance sign convention uses positive variance to indicate actual exceeded estimate for revenue/income items, with brackets or color coding to distinguish favorable vs. unfavorable.
Balance sheet items (Assets, Equity, Cash) are explicitly presented as period-end snapshots dated March 31, 2026.
EBITDA is excluded from the variance table, consistent with the requirement that the 10-Q does not directly report it.
All XBRL-sourced actual figures include a cross-reference to their EDGAR line-item tags for auditability.
The filing date (May 6, 2026) for the AMZN 10-Q is referenced.
The company is identified by its full legal name Amazon.com, Inc. and ticker AMZN.
The employer (Brennan Brothers & Co.) is referenced in the deliverable header or context.
The analyst (Henrik Ådahl) and/or managing director (Kara Vossberg) are identified.
The deliverable date or timeframe (Q1 2026, as of March 31, 2026) is clearly stated.
Formulas in the Excel workbook are transparent and auditable (e.g., cells reference other cells rather than containing hardcoded results).
The stale XBRL Gross Profit figure of $5,531M (dated 2009-12-31) is explicitly identified as an anomaly and excluded or corrected.
Revenue from the EDGAR source is correctly tagged as RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax.
Cost of goods and services sold is correctly tagged as CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold.
Operating income is correctly tagged as OperatingIncomeLoss.
Net income is correctly tagged as NetIncomeLoss.
Diluted EPS is correctly tagged as EarningsPerShareDiluted.
Total assets is correctly tagged as Assets.
Stockholders' equity is correctly tagged as StockholdersEquity.
Cash and cash equivalents is correctly tagged as CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue.
The CIK number 0001018724 for Amazon is referenced or implied in the data sourcing.
The analysis uses a Q1 quarterly basis (not cumulative YTD) consistent with the original model.
The deliverable uses the stale Gross Profit value of $5,531M as the actual Q1 2026 figure without correction.
The deliverable is provided in a format other than .xlsx (e.g., PDF, CSV).
The executive summary identifies the three largest absolute-dollar variances by line item name and dollar amount.
The assignment date (May 13, 2026) is referenced in the deliverable header or metadata.
The deadline (May 17, 2026) is referenced or the deliverable is dated within the required timeframe.
The sector classification (retail_ecom) for Amazon is noted or implied.

explicit_requirements: Build a variance analysis table comparing Brennan Brothers' Q1 2026 estimates for AMZN against the actual reported figures from the May 6, 10-Q filing for Revenue, COGS, Gross Profit, Operating Income, Net Income, EPS (diluted), Total Assets, Stockholders' Equity, and Cash & Cash Equivalents.
Calculate both the absolute dollar variance and the percentage variance (actual vs. estimate) for each line item.

Flag any line item where the percentage variance exceeds ±5% and provide a one-sentence driver explanation sourced from management commentary in the filing or identifiable from the financials themselves.
Include a reconciliation bridge showing how Gross Profit flows from Revenue minus COGS for both the estimate and the actual, ensuring internal consistency.
Present EPS diluted on a per-share basis consistent with the filing's 2.78 USD/share figure and reconcile share count differences if any exist between estimate and actual.
Summarize the top three largest absolute-dollar variances in a brief executive summary paragraph at the top of the deliverable.
Ensure all dollar figures are displayed in millions (USD) with one decimal place, consistent with standard sell-side formatting conventions.
Include a column showing the consensus sell-side mean estimate if available from public sources, adding a third column for a three-way comparison (Brennan Brothers estimate vs. consensus vs. actual).
implicit_requirements: Variance sign convention: positive variance means actual exceeded estimate (favorable for revenue/income items, unfavorable for cost items); use brackets or color coding to distinguish favorable vs. unfavorable.
The deliverable must follow Brennan Brothers' internal template formatting — blue font for hardcoded inputs, black for calculated cells, and no merged cells in data ranges.
EBITDA should be excluded unless Brennan Brothers' original model included it, since the 10-Q does not directly report EBITDA.
Balance sheet items (Assets, Equity, Cash) should be presented as period-end snapshots (March 31, 2026), not quarterly flows.
All XBRL-sourced figures should be cross-referenced to their EDGAR line-item tags for auditability.
The analysis should use the TTM (trailing twelve months) or Q1 quarterly basis as specified in the original Brennan Brothers model, not a cumulative YTD basis.

reference_answer.narrative_prompt:
You are an associate analyst at an investment bank. You have built a 5-year unlevered DCF model for AMAZON.COM, INC. (AMZN) based on its latest SEC filings.

The model includes:
- Base-year financials from EDGAR XBRL
- Revenue growth assumption of 3.8% (sector-typical for retail_ecom)
- WACC of 10.56% derived from beta=1.13, Rf=4.35%, ERP=5.50%
- Terminal growth of 2.00%

Write a one-page summary memo explaining the key assumptions and valuation conclusion. Be specific with numbers. Do NOT use AI hedging.
